# FormLabel accessibility conformance

Rated against WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA. See the [reports legend](../accessibility.md).

<!-- intro:start -->

FormLabel labels a field or, as a `legend`, names a group. It is not focusable. A click on a label with `htmlFor` focuses or activates its field, so the field report rates the keyboard, focus, and pointer criteria.

<!-- intro:end -->

| Result                | Count |
| :-------------------- | :---- |
| ✅ Supports           | 11    |
| ⚠️ Partially Supports | 2     |
| ❌ Does Not Support   | 0     |
| ➖ Not Applicable     | 42    |
| 🚩 Flagged            | 3/13  |

## Known gaps

- ⚠️ **1.3.1 Info and Relationships.** <!-- 1.3.1:gap:start -->On a `required` group legend, the asterisk is `aria-hidden`, and Checkbox, Radio, and Switch do not take `required` from FormControl. Assistive technology then gets no required state.<!-- 1.3.1:gap:end -->
- ⚠️ **1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum).** <!-- 1.4.3:gap:start -->A focused label takes the `main` color of its field. In light mode, `info` (`3.86:1`) and `warning` (`3.11:1`) are less than `4.5:1`. In dark mode, the error label falls below `4.5:1` on a Paper with elevation 2 or more, such as a Menu or Dialog, because the elevation overlay lightens the surface.<!-- 1.4.3:gap:end -->

## Success criteria

### 🔍 Manual

#### 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence · A

`✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.3.2:start -->

- The label renders its text, then the asterisk when `required`. The asterisk is `aria-hidden`.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Read a form with a screen reader in browse mode.
2. Compare the reading order of each label and its field with the visual order.

<!-- 1.3.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.2:pass:start -->each label comes before its field in the reading order.<!-- 1.3.2:pass:end -->

#### 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics · A

`✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.3.3:start -->

- The label is text. Instructions in the page must not refer to a field only by its position or color.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Find product copy that refers to a form field.
2. Make sure that it names the field by its label.

<!-- 1.3.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.3:pass:start -->each instruction names the field by its label.<!-- 1.3.3:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.5 Images of Text · AA

`✅ Supports` · `○ Author`

<!-- 1.4.5:start -->

- The label is real text.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Select the text of a label with the mouse.

<!-- 1.4.5:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.5:pass:start -->the mouse selects the label text character by character.<!-- 1.4.5:pass:end -->

### 🔁 Hybrid

#### 1.3.1 Info and Relationships · A

`🚩` · `⚠️ Partially Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `FormLabel.test.js`

<!-- 1.3.1:start -->

- The root is a `<label>` and sets no `htmlFor` of its own. The author connects it to the field with `htmlFor` and `id`. As the first `legend` of a `fieldset`, for example in `FormControl component="fieldset"`, it names the group. For a RadioGroup, the author can also give the label an `id` and set `aria-labelledby` on the group. Unit tests confirm that FormLabel renders a `legend` element that names the group, and forwards `htmlFor` as the `for` attribute.
- Inside a `FormControl`, the label takes the `required`, `error`, `disabled`, and `focused` states of the field. The field itself must expose these states.
- Only fields based on InputBase take `required` from FormControl: Input, OutlinedInput, FilledInput, and Select. Checkbox, Radio, and Switch do not, and RadioGroup has no `required` prop. On a `required` group legend, the asterisk is `aria-hidden`, so assistive technology gets no required state. A unit test confirms this gap for Checkbox.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Start a screen reader (NVDA with Chrome, or VoiceOver with Safari).
2. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> into a group with `FormLabel component="legend"`.
3. Listen to the announcement.
4. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to a field labeled with `htmlFor`, and listen again.

<!-- 1.3.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.3.1:pass:start -->the screen reader announces the legend as the group name, and the label as the name of the field.<!-- 1.3.1:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.1 Use of Color · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 1.4.1:start -->

- In the error state, the label turns red. The color is not the only cue when a text message or an icon also shows the error. The author adds it, for example with a FormHelperText.
- The asterisk shows the required state with a glyph, not with color.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Put a field in the error state.
2. In Chrome DevTools, open the Rendering tab, and select Emulate vision deficiencies > Achromatopsia.
3. Make sure that a text message or an icon also shows the error.

<!-- 1.4.1:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.1:pass:start -->a text message or an icon, not only the red label, shows the error.<!-- 1.4.1:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) · AA

`⚠️ Partially Supports` · `● Component`

Tested by: unit `FormLabel.test.js` · axe-core `color-contrast` ❌

<!-- 1.4.3:start -->

- Label colors against the page background:

  | State                | Light mode (`#fff`) | Dark mode (`#121212`) |
  | :------------------- | ------------------: | --------------------: |
  | Resting              |              5.74:1 |                9.43:1 |
  | Focused, `primary`   |              4.60:1 |               10.71:1 |
  | Focused, `secondary` |              6.30:1 |                7.84:1 |
  | Focused, `info`      |              3.86:1 |                8.13:1 |
  | Focused, `success`   |              5.13:1 |                7.92:1 |
  | Focused, `warning`   |              3.11:1 |                9.64:1 |
  | Error                |              4.98:1 |                5.09:1 |

- A unit test compares the focused colors with the [palette contrast contract](../../test/contrastContract.ts). Only `info` and `warning` fail. axe-core `color-contrast` fails on the light color fixture. It passes on the dark one and on the states fixture, which has the error and disabled labels.
- In dark mode, a Paper lightens its surface with an elevation overlay. The error label is about `4.52:1` on a Card at its default elevation 1. On a Paper with elevation 2 or more, such as a Menu or Dialog, it falls below `4.5:1`: about `4.30:1` at elevation 2, `3.68:1` at elevation 8 (Menu), and `3.13:1` at elevation 24 (Dialog). A unit test confirms elevation 2 and 24.
- A disabled label is `text.disabled` (`2.68:1` light, `5.32:1` dark). When the field is also disabled, the label is part of an inactive component, so 1.4.3 does not apply.

**Manual testing steps**

1. With a contrast checker, measure the label in the resting, focused, and error states, for each `color` in use.
2. Switch to dark mode and measure again.
3. Measure the error label inside a Menu and a Dialog in dark mode.

<!-- 1.4.3:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.3:pass:start -->each label is at least `4.5:1` in light and dark mode.<!-- 1.4.3:pass:end -->

#### 2.4.6 Headings and Labels · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

<!-- 2.4.6:start -->

- The label text describes the field. Whether it is clear is an authoring concern.

**Manual testing steps**

<!-- 2.4.6:end -->

#### 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions · A

`🚩` · `✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `FormLabel.test.js` · axe-core `form-field-multiple-labels` ✅

<!-- 3.3.2:start -->

- The label is the visible instruction for the field. With `required`, it shows an asterisk, which is `aria-hidden`.
- The screen reader announces "required" from the field. Inside a `FormControl` with `required`, the label shows the asterisk and an Input gets the `required` attribute. A unit test confirms this. Checkbox, Radio, and Switch do not, see 1.3.1. Set `aria-required="true"` on a RadioGroup, or `required` on a single Checkbox or Switch. `required` on each checkbox of a group makes every box mandatory, so for a checkbox group, state the requirement in the legend text.
- The author tells the user what the asterisk means, for example at the top of the form.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Render a required Input and a required radio group with `FormLabel component="legend"`. Set `aria-required="true"` on the RadioGroup, because RadioGroup does not take `required` from FormControl (see 1.3.1).
2. Make sure that the asterisk shows after each label.
3. Start a screen reader.
4. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to each field.
5. Listen to the announcement.

<!-- 3.3.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 3.3.2:pass:start -->the asterisk shows. The screen reader announces "required" for each field. It does not announce "star".<!-- 3.3.2:pass:end -->

#### 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: axe-core `aria-allowed-attr` ✅, `aria-conditional-attr` ✅, `aria-deprecated-role` ✅, `aria-hidden-focus` ✅, `aria-prohibited-attr` ✅, `aria-required-attr` ✅, `aria-roles` ✅, `aria-valid-attr` ✅, `aria-valid-attr-value` ✅, `duplicate-id-aria` ✅, `label` ✅, `nested-interactive` ✅

<!-- 4.1.2:start -->

- The label gives the accessible name of the field or group. axe-core `label` and the ARIA rules pass on the fixtures.
- The role and state come from the field, not from the label.

**Manual testing steps**

1. With a screen reader, press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to each labeled field.
2. Listen to its name.

<!-- 4.1.2:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 4.1.2:pass:start -->each field announces the text of its FormLabel as its name.<!-- 4.1.2:pass:end -->

### ⚙️ Automated

#### 1.4.4 Resize Text · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.4:start -->

- The label uses the `body1` typography, set in `rem`, and wraps. A Playwright test confirms that the states fixture does not overflow or clip at a 200% text size.
- The 1.4.10 test at 320 px also covers full-page zoom up to 400%.

**Manual testing steps**

1. Set the browser page zoom to 200%.
2. Look at each label in a form.

<!-- 1.4.4:end -->

**Pass:** <!-- 1.4.4:pass:start -->each label is fully visible. No text is cut off or overlaps.<!-- 1.4.4:pass:end -->

#### 1.4.10 Reflow · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.10:start -->

- The label wraps with its container. A Playwright test confirms the states fixture at a 320 px viewport.

<!-- 1.4.10:end -->

#### 1.4.12 Text Spacing · AA

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: Playwright

<!-- 1.4.12:end -->

#### 2.5.3 Label in Name · A

`✅ Supports` · `◐ Shared`

Tested by: unit `FormLabel.test.js`

<!-- 2.5.3:start -->

- The visible label is the accessible name of the field. The `required` asterisk is hidden, so it adds nothing to the name. A unit test confirms this.

## Not applicable

- **1.1.1 Non-text Content (A).** <!-- 1.1.1:start -->The label renders no non-text content. The required `*` is decorative (`aria-hidden`) text that duplicates the native `required` state of the field. On a group legend, nothing duplicates the asterisk, see 1.3.1.<!-- 1.1.1:end -->
- **1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (A), 1.2.4 Captions (Live) (AA), 1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded) (AA).** No audio or video.
- **1.3.4 Orientation (AA).** Sets no orientation lock; a layout concern.
- **1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (AA).** Collects no information about the user through `autocomplete`.
- **1.4.2 Audio Control (A).** Emits no audio.
- **1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (AA).** <!-- 1.4.11:start -->The label renders no graphical object and no component boundary. The asterisk is text.<!-- 1.4.11:end -->
- **1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (AA).** Shows no additional content on hover or focus; a `Tooltip` wrapper would own this.
- **2.1.1 Keyboard (A), 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap (A), 2.4.3 Focus Order (A), 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA), 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) (AA), 3.2.1 On Focus (A), 3.2.2 On Input (A).** <!-- 2.1.1,2.1.2,2.4.3,2.4.7,2.4.11,3.2.1,3.2.2:start -->The label is not focusable. The field it labels covers these.<!-- 2.1.1,2.1.2,2.4.3,2.4.7,2.4.11,3.2.1,3.2.2:end -->
- **2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts (A).** Binds no single-character keyboard shortcut.
- **2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (A).** Sets no time limit.
- **2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (A).** No auto-starting moving, blinking, or auto-updating content.
- **2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold (A).** Nothing flashes.
- **2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (A), 2.4.2 Page Titled (A), 2.4.5 Multiple Ways (AA).** Page or site structure, not a single component.
- **2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) (A).** The component renders no links.
- **2.5.1 Pointer Gestures (A), 2.5.4 Motion Actuation (A).** Activates on a simple click; reads no device motion.
- **2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation (A), 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) (AA).** <!-- 2.5.2,2.5.8:start -->A label with `htmlFor` adds its area to the target of its field. It is not a separate target. The field report rates these criteria.<!-- 2.5.2,2.5.8:end -->
- **2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA).** No drag interactions.
- **3.1.1 Language of Page (A), 3.1.2 Language of Parts (AA).** The component emits no `<html lang>` and no text of its own. A foreign-language label is the author's phrase to mark.
- **3.2.3 Consistent Navigation (AA).** Covers repeated navigation across a set of pages, not a single component.
- **3.2.4 Consistent Identification (AA).** <!-- 3.2.4:start -->The label is not interactive. Each control report rates 3.2.4 for the control and its label.<!-- 3.2.4:end -->
- **3.2.6 Consistent Help (A).** Covers consistent placement of help across pages.
- **3.3.1 Error Identification (A), 3.3.3 Error Suggestion (AA), 3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data) (AA).** Collects and validates no input; these belong to the form or process.
- **3.3.7 Redundant Entry (A).** Captures no previously entered data to repopulate.
- **3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) (AA).** No authentication step; the duty falls on the credential fields.
- **4.1.3 Status Messages (AA).** Emits no status messages; state changes are covered by 4.1.2.

## Level AAA

<!-- level-aaa:start -->

- **1.4.6 Contrast (Enhanced), 7:1.** In light mode, the resting label (`5.74:1`), every focused color, and the error color are less than 7:1. `🚩`

<!-- level-aaa:end -->

## Scope and test environment

- **Standard.** WCAG 2.2, Level A and AA.
- **Component version.** `@mui/material` 10.0.0-alpha.0.

<!-- scope:start -->

- **Scope.** The FormLabel component, as a field label and as a group legend, rendered through its documented API.
- **Automated.** axe-core in the Playwright test harness, on the FormLabel fixtures in [`form-label.a11y.json`](../../../../docs/data/material/components/form-label/form-label.a11y.json). Tests are in `FormLabel.test.js`.
- **Assistive-technology review.** Not done yet. The flagged criteria come from a review of the source. A review with NVDA, JAWS, and VoiceOver must still confirm them.

<!-- scope:end -->
